name: Unconstrained Face Detection and Open-Set Face Recognition Challenge
description:
Face detection and recognition benchmarks have shifted toward more difficult
environments. The challenge presented in this paper addresses the next step in
the direction of automatic detection and identification of people from outdoor
surveillance cameras. While face detection has shown remarkable success in
images collected from the web, surveillance cameras include more diverse
occlusions, poses, weather conditions and image blur. Although face
verification or closed-set face identification have surpassed human
capabilities on some datasets, open-set identification is much more complex as
it needs to reject both unknown identities and false accepts from the face
detector. We show that unconstrained face detection can approach high detection
rates albeit with moderate false accept rates. By contrast, open-set face
recognition is currently weak and requires much more attention.
evaluation_method: detection: mAP / detection rate vs false accept rate; open-set recognition: TPIR@FPIR (true positive identification rate at fixed false positive identification rate)
general_score_metric: mAP (for detection) and TPIR@FPIR (for open-set identification)
typical_sota_score: detection mAP often in the ~80–95% range on related benchmarks; open-set recognition performance is substantially lower (TPIR often <50% depending on FPIR)
reputation: Influential within the face recognition and surveillance research community for highlighting challenges of unconstrained, open-set scenarios, but specialized and sensitive in application.
notes: Contains surveillance-style, unconstrained imagery with heavy occlusions/blur—raises privacy and bias concerns; open-set recognition remains an unsolved/low-performing problem compared to closed-set benchmarks; not saturated.
